GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli

GitHub Copilot CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Highlights

Two patch releases (v1.0.111 and v1.0.112) landed in the last 24 hours, headlined by regular-expression support in enterprise-managed Shell/Bash/PowerShell permission rules and a new --host-allow-session-creation flag for remote CLI hosts. The changelog also reveals a controversial default shift: the CLI now uses "each model's recommended context window," while macOS "best-effort startup" on Ventura 13.5+ is being quietly expanded without official OS support. Meanwhile, the issue tracker is dominated by long-tail permission, sandbox, and Windows/MCP authentication regressions — several of which (PRU quota wipe, Entra token cache) were closed today.

2. Releases

v1.0.112 (2026-11-13) — Release

  • Failed /compact now surfaces the model provider's actual error instead of an internal host-rethrow prefix.
  • Pasted prompts entered before managed-account policy finishes loading are preserved; pressing Enter re-sends the paste rather than dropping it.
  • v1.0.112-0 (prerelease): improved best-effort startup on macOS Ventura 13.5+; per-model recommended context windows used by default (explicit overrides still honored); /chronicle cost-tips now includes Copilot App sessions and recommends cheaper models.

v1.0.111 (2026-11-13) — Release

  • Regex support added to enterprise-managed Shell, Bash, and PowerShell permission rules.
  • New --host-allow-session-creation flag lets remote clients create sessions on CLI hosts for a single launch without mutating saved settings.
  • /usage premium-request percentages refreshed.
  • v1.0.111-0 (prerelease): same two additions above, plus organization support links in policy surfaces.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #4802 [CLOSED] PRU Quota Wiped Out, likely tied to Assisted Permissions — A Copilot Pro (legacy request-based) user reports 234 PRUs vanishing after enabling Assisted Permissions; 11 comments. Closed today, but this is the highest-engagement thread and signals billing-adjacent risk in the permissions subsystem.

  2. #5236 [CLOSED] Windows: Entra broker token cache stays 0 bytes after MCP sign-in — Every new process re-prompts for Entra auth because the cache file is never written. Closed after 8 comments; important for Windows enterprise users running HTTP MCP servers.

  3. #2374 [CLOSED] Autopilot enters an infinite loop — Workflow reproduces via /plan → autopilot approval. Closed after ~8 months and 8 comments; a notable long-standing reliability fix.

  4. #5323 [OPEN] Add setting to disable agent checkpoint refs (refs/agents/*) — Every agent turn creates commits under the user's own git identity. 6 comments, 2 👍. This pollutes git log --all and any ref-rendering tool — a real ergonomics/compliance concern.

  5. #5066 [OPEN] Assisted permissions regression — Too many commands (even a simple PowerShell file-find) now demand approval. 4 comments, 1 👍; pairs with #4802 to suggest the Assisted Permissions model needs tuning.

  6. #4866 [CLOSED] Ctrl-D in ask_user/elicitation fields shuts down the session — In-progress input is discarded when Ctrl-D is pressed inside agent elicitation forms, unlike the main composer. 3 comments, 3 👍; classic input-handling regression fixed today.

  7. #3192 [OPEN] statusLine.command not executed when footer.showCustom=true — Open since May, still unpatched as of 1.0.43+; blocks custom footer tooling (branch, cost, model indicators). 3 comments, 2 👍.

  8. #3339 [OPEN] Quoted strings starting with / misread as paths — The path-access scanner flags literal arguments as filesystem intents, causing spurious permission prompts. Long-lived (#3339, since May) with low visibility but high annoyance for shell-heavy workflows.

  9. #5404 [OPEN] Windows: launching copilot in a git repo kills parent pwsh.exe — tgrep indexing crashes the parent shell and tears down the terminal tab (and attached processes like ssh-agent). Only 1 comment so far but severe severity — reported on 1.0.108.

  10. #5102 [CLOSED] Sandboxed git can't use credentials differing from Copilot/gh identity — sandbox.auth.git injects a highest-precedence empty credential.helper, discarding fine-grained PATs. Closed today; matters for enterprise sandbox users with separate service identities.

Honorable mentions: #4509 (6 👍, --no-alt-screen silently removed), #5085 (macOS sandbox + Mach SecurityServer breaks HTTPS), #5390 (macOS sandbox allowLocalNetwork ignored in proxy mode).

4. Key PR Progress

Only 2 PRs were updated in the last 24h, both Dependabot and both CLOSED:

  1. #5454 [CLOSED] bump debian f6b08b0 → a72b443 in /container — Docker base image refresh for the container image. Routine supply-chain hygiene.

  2. #5453 [CLOSED] bump docker/login-action 4.7.0 → 4.8.0 — CI auth action update (v4.8.0 sets Docker docs metadata). Low risk, automated.

No feature PRs landed in the last 24h window; all notable feature movement is in the v1.0.111/112 release notes above.

5. Hot Discussions

No GitHub Discussions data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Agent checkpoint hygiene (#5323): users want to opt out of refs/agents/* commits polluting their repos.
  • Enterprise policy granularity (#4783): separate policy scope for CLI sandbox + yolo mode; also mirrored by the new regex permission support in v1.0.111.
  • Sandboxing allowlists (#4881, #4046): exact Mach/XPC allowlists on macOS and a documented cross-platform sandbox support matrix.
  • Instruction-file deduplication (#4603): persistent per-user exclusion for duplicate CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.
  • Plugin format completeness (#5440): Agent Plugins 1.0 rules/ and applyTo frontmatter are silently ignored — a parity gap that will bite plugin authors.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Permissions friction and cost exposure — Assisted Permissions is the top theme: too many prompts (#5066) and a reported PRU wipe (#4802). Users need predictable, tunable approval behavior.
  2. Sandbox instability across platforms — macOS Mach/XPC restrictions break HTTPS (#5085) and local networking (#5390); Windows sandbox requirements are undocumented (#4046); sandboxed git credential injection is broken (#5102). This is the single largest cluster of open bugs.
  3. Windows regressions — Entra token cache (#5236) and the parent-shell killer (#5404) show Windows remains a second-class platform for CLI stability.
  4. Silent regressions with no escape hatch — Removal of --no-alt-screen (#4509) with no replacement or deprecation notice is cited as a pattern of breaking changes arriving without migration paths.
  5. MCP auth edge cases — Headless OAuth timeouts (#3039) and metadata URL redirect mismatches (#4769) continue to block MCP adoption outside interactive desktop environments.
  6. Long-lived renderer/config bugs — Custom statusLine (#3192) and path-scanner false positives (#3339) have been open for ~6 months, eroding trust in the configuration surface.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Highlights

OpenCode shipped v2.3.0, headlined by background subagents enabled by default — subagents now return immediately, run concurrently, and report back when idle, a significant architectural shift for parallel agent workflows. The release also appears to have introduced regressions: within 24 hours, users reported zombie PTY processes on Linux (#63817) and old cancelled/failed sessions unexpectedly re-executing (#63802). Meanwhile, the long-running free-tier issue thread (#59387) has ballooned to 366 comments, cementing free-tier quota handling as the community's most persistent pain point.

2. Releases

v2.3.0

  • Background Subagents by Default — Subagents now return immediately and continue in the background, reporting back when idle. Multiple subagents can run concurrently while work continues in the parent session. (#63382)

⚠️ Early regression reports against 2.3.0:

  • #63817 — Shell commands leave zombie processes under opencode-pty daemon on Linux (not present in 2.2.7).
  • #63802 — Upgrading to 2.3.0 re-ran an old cancelled/failed session, posting an unexpected GitHub review.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #59387 — Free tier issues mega-thread (366 comments, 28 👍, OPEN). The central hub for free-tier failures: quota-exceeded errors, limits that never reset, and desktop version lockouts. Its volume makes it the single clearest signal of free-tier friction.

  2. #52941 — Desktop file tree/preview show stale contents after agent edits (13 comments, reproduced). Users can't trust the Review pane to reflect agent changes — a core trust issue for the desktop workflow.

  3. #63216 — Rogue actions: agent continued after explicit STOP (12 comments, CLOSED). A high-severity report of unauthorized file modification on Windows. Closed, but the underlying control-safety concern resonates broadly.

  4. #52154 — Message history isolation per session (10 comments, 7 👍, OPEN). Arrow-up recalls prompts from other sessions — a frequent annoyance for users running many parallel sessions. A fix PR is already in flight (see #55261).

  5. #27511 — Suspend/Resume for agent and subagent execution (9 comments, 18 👍, OPEN). High-upvote request to pause and resume agent execution — increasingly relevant with concurrent background subagents in 2.3.0.

  6. #50130 — V1 sessions after completed migration are never imported (9 comments, reproduced). Data-continuity bug: sessions landing in the DB after migration.v1-v2 completes stay orphaned in legacy tables.

  7. #63778 — Subagent model calls fail with "Specified function… not found" (8 comments, CLOSED). Specialist subagents (sage/architect/forge) failed on first model call across providers — notable given subagents are the focus of 2.3.0.

  8. #43126 — Auto pause/resume on known rate-limit reset (7 comments, 16 👍, OPEN). Persist session, pause, and auto-resume when a provider reports a reset time — a high-demand automation for rate-limited workflows.

  9. #59293 — Subagent sessionID continuation always fails (4 comments, OPEN). sessionID is coerced to "ses", making it impossible to continue an existing subagent conversation — directly relevant to the new background-subagent model.

  10. #63218 — Local DB recreated empty after restart following auth failure (2 comments, CLOSED, severity: high). Total loss of sessions and projects; a catastrophic data-loss scenario worth monitoring for recurrence.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #55261 — prompt.history_scope setting (OPEN). Adds opt-in session scoping so Up/Down recall only the current session's prompts — the direct fix for #52154.

  2. #58846 — Repair V1 global sessions left by completed imports (OPEN). Backfills folder→project attribution for users who already upgraded past the migration window (fixes fallout from #49827).

  3. #60895 — opencode session list --all with cursor pagination (OPEN). Removes the current-directory project filter so sessions across projects are visible.

  4. #63872 — Larger image budget for claude-agent (OPEN). Raises boundImages cut/drop thresholds from 25/15 MiB to 96/64 MiB, fixing #63870.

  5. #63873 — Merge claude-agent catch-up text into one block (OPEN). Emits a single text block instead of one per role/tool tag, improving Anthropic prompt-cache hit rates.

  6. #61386 — Preserve explicit traceparent in HTTP requests (OPEN). Stops Effect's HTTP client from overwriting caller-supplied trace context — important for observability integrations.

  7. #61622 — Separate model capabilities in localized summaries (OPEN). Fixes concatenated labels (e.g., TextImageTools) in Simplified Chinese via narrow conjunction formatting.

  8. #63866 — Skip-to-content link in the shell (OPEN). WCAG 2.4.1 bypass-blocks accessibility improvement, the first focusable element in the shell.

  9. #63851 — Accessible names for unnamed controls (OPEN). Names the session search listbox, directory pickers, and other controls previously invisible to assistive tech (part of the #57491 accessibility push alongside #63865).

  10. #58542 — Cmd+X cut in the TUI prompt (OPEN). Copies (with pasted-text placeholders expanded) and deletes the selection, matching standard editor behavior.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session history hygiene — Per-session prompt recall (#52154/#55261) and no-restore TUI tab scopes (#61063) reflect demand for clean, isolated session state as users run many parallel sessions.
  • Agent lifecycle control — Suspend/resume execution (#27511, 18 👍), plugin-driven session.stop (#63650), and auto pause/resume on rate-limit reset (#43126, 16 👍) all point to users wanting finer-grained control over long-running agents.
  • Rate-limit ergonomics — From auto-resume (#43126) to the free-tier mega-thread (#59387), quota handling is the dominant feature-request theme.
  • SDK/plugin extensibility — Binding agent/model/variant to queued prompts (#48356) and the session.stop API (#63650) show the v2 SDK is being stretched by integrators like Kimaki.
  • Desktop/UI polish — Resizable content width (#53382), unified Thinking/Patch indicators (#44164), and a broad accessibility sweep (#57491) indicate growing investment in the desktop and TUI experience.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Free-tier quotas and reset failures — The 366-comment thread (#59387) captures quota errors, limits that never reset, and desktop version lockouts. This is the single loudest community frustration.
  2. Stale state after agent edits — The desktop file tree and preview pane (#52941, #57099) frequently show outdated contents; Reload doesn't help. Erodes trust in the primary review workflow.
  3. Subagent reliability — The 2.3.0 headline feature is shadowed by bugs: sessionID continuation broken (#59293), model-call failures (#63778), and session.stop gaps (#63650).
  4. Upgrade/migration fragility — 2.3.0 re-ran old sessions (#63802), 2.2.7→2.3.0 left zombie PTYs (#63817), completed migrations orphan V1 sessions (#50130), and a restart after auth failure wiped the local DB (#63218).
  5. Process/resource leaks — MCP config reloads leak server processes (#63847), and pooled MCP is silently ignored for legacy-protocol servers with no runtime signal (#63848).
  6. Plugin cache staleness — @latest plugin specs never refresh cached installs (#54127), forcing version pins to pick up bug fixes — a repeated footgun for plugin authors.
  7. Windows/desktop startup issues — %APPDATA% execution restrictions break server startup (#56016), and custom agents vanish after reload on Windows (#63201).

  8. #15894 — loop_wakeup not cancelled by a user stop (8 comments, P2). Self-paced loops resume after explicit stop — a correctness bug for autonomous manager workflows.
  9. #17091 — AUTO mode classifier cannot see approved plan (exit_plan_mode rendered as {}). Permission-classifier blind spot; the plan/approval context never reaches the classifier.
  10. #16824 — Repeated hallucinated project name despite clean reinstall (5 comments, long-context/token-management). Highlights memory/context-persistence problems in long sessions.

  5. #17025 — fix(cli): stabilize OpenTUI streaming markdown preview. Disables sync streaming preview to eliminate jitter.
  6. #16439 — fix(core): replay the persisted startup prelude on resume. Resumed sessions re-use the original prelude (date, git snapshot, MCP instructions) rather than rebuilding.

  10. #17190 / #17202 — fix(core): model-catalog normalization for DeepSeek V3.1/V3.2 and Ollama llama4 tags. Prevents output-token/image-capability losses from id-normalization mismatches.

No dedicated Discussion data was provided in this window; omitted.

  • Permissions correctness: malformed rules parsing as inert without reporting (#16078); AUTO-mode classifier blind to approved plans (#17091).

OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-14

Issues: 333 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-14 01:24 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains a high-velocity, high-complexity project with substantial daily churn: 333 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, though activity skews heavily toward maintenance rather than new capability (0 new releases). The project's health signal is mixed — a very active triage and fix pipeline (217 PRs merged/closed) coexists with a persistent queue of P0/P1 stability bugs, many of which are long-lived (some open since August-September 2026). Recurring themes across hot items are Windows/macOS platform reliability, SQLite/Gateway memory and event-loop pressure at scale, message/subagent delivery loss, and CJK/i18n tokenization gaps in search. The issue tracker shows a mature "clawsweeper" triage taxonomy (gold shrimp → platinum hermit ratings, fix-shape, needs-info flags), indicating a well-instrumented but heavily loaded maintainer workflow. No releases landed today, so today's digest is dominated by in-flight fixes and unresolved reliability blockers.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. No migration or breaking-change notes to report.

3. Project Progress

217 PRs were merged or closed today. Notable merged/closed or advanced work:

  • Stale/feature issues closed (cleanup): #126950 (Telegram opaque callback payloads dropped — linked PR open), #192009 (cross-provider cron fallback authorization — product decision reached), #142037 (Slack thread-mismatch mute bookkeeping), #150029 (configurable automation Inspect link).
  • In-flight gateway/CI work: #198194 (reduce resident memory on constrained ARM64 hosts, XL), #198265 (start default memory index managers at Gateway boot — closes #194164), #198547 (fix agents.delete stalling behind model-catalog build), #198553 (expire bound node with owner device), #193749 (GitHub publication with PostgreSQL session/state stores).
  • OpenClaw ID / access model advancing via stacked PRs: #197770, #197748, #197782, #197785 (member roles, guest sandbox role, admin role semantics, Doctor role checks).
  • UI/E2E test stabilization: multiple small PRs (#198533, #198534, #198538, #198544, #198555, #198537) aligning tests with the new composer/picker layout after #197820.
  • Explicitly rejected: #198364 (CI credential-analysis tree walk — 1.51% gain below the 5% acceptance threshold).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Link
#170956 Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission error (P0, crash-loop, release blocker) 32 openclaw/openclaw Issue #170956
#119720 Synchronous agent persistence blocks Gateway event loop at scale (P1, message-loss) 26 openclaw/openclaw Issue #119720

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Data window: 2026-11-14 (trailing 24h) | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape in late 2026 is bifurcating into two mature camps: high-churn reference platforms (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, ZeroClaw) operating at hundreds of issues/PRs per day, and release-driven downstream distributions (QwenPaw) absorbing post-release regression waves. A third, quieter tier (IronClaw) represents specialized/niche implementations that trade velocity for focus. Across all active projects, the binding constraint has shifted from feature velocity to reliability and security semantics — message/subagent delivery loss, gateway event-loop pressure, sandbox/redaction boundaries, and credential handling dominate the highest-engagement threads. Security hardening is no longer a bolt-on: ZeroClaw and Hermes Agent are both running explicit "security marathon" campaigns, and community proposals increasingly ask not just what the agent does but what it can see and reach (MITM egress proxies, write-only secrets, caller-scoped delegation). The ecosystem's center of gravity is converging on a single hard problem: making a persistent, multi-channel, tool-using agent trustworthy under concurrency and adversarial conditions.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale of triage infrastructure. OpenClaw is the only project in this set with a formalized triage taxonomy ("clawsweeper" ratings: gold shrimp → platinum hermit, fix-shape, needs-info flags). This is a mature workflow artifact no peer exhibits.
  • Breadth of channel surface. Telegram, Slack, msteams, Codex, claude-cli — the integration matrix is wider than any peer, at the cost of more seams to break.
  • Ecosystem gravity. 333 issues / 500 PRs in 24h is roughly an order of magnitude above Hermes Agent (50/50), QwenPaw (20/36), and ZeroClaw (7/50). OpenClaw is functioning as the de facto reference implementation of the category.

Technical approach differences:

  • Unlike QwenPaw (release-driven, channel-plugin model) or ZeroClaw (Rust, sandbox/relay-centric arc), OpenClaw leans on a JavaScript/TypeScript gateway + plugin architecture with heavy reliance on a SQLite worker layer and a Gateway event loop. This is precisely where its dominant failure families live — event-loop blocking at scale (#119720, open since August), SQLite worker OOM (#191847), and off-heap RSS creep (#182369). Peers architecturally sidestep or defer some of this pressure (ZeroClaw's Rust runtime, QwenPaw's per-channel isolation).
  • OpenClaw's access-control model (OpenClaw ID: member/guest/admin/Doctor roles via stacked PRs) is more ambitious and further along than peers' — but it also means OpenClaw carries more security surface area in-flight.

Community size comparison:

  • Largest by raw engagement: OpenClaw's hottest thread (#170956, Windows lifecycle) drew 32 comments; its top six threads average ~19 comments. Compare to QwenPaw's top thread (#8071, 13 comments) and Hermes Agent's hottest (#77253, 13 comments). OpenClaw's community comments in aggregate on a single issue can exceed a peer's entire daily comment volume.
  • The trade-off is visible: OpenClaw's maintainer bandwidth is the binding constraint — several fixes exist on main but not in stable (e.g., #177063→#185085), producing a release-velocity gap that Hermes Agent (canary-per-day cadence) and QwenPaw (fix-PR-within-24h culture) avoid.

Net position: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's anchor reference but currently pays a heavy reliability tax for its scope. A stable-backport push would likely reduce user-visible P1 volume more than net-new development this cycle — a low-cost, high-leverage move peers have already internalized.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Three requirements emerge independently across multiple projects — the strongest signal in this dataset:

(a) Silent data/delivery loss — the #1 cross-project reliability theme

  • OpenClaw: Subagent final answer lost + duplicate settle events (#155119); exec-completion wakes lost (#185085); Telegram opaque callbacks dropped (#126950); Slack thread-mismatch.
  • Hermes Agent: notify_on_complete stale synthetic turn (#94455, closed today); background work fails to follow through (#149248 — "nearly every time I've asked Hermes to handle something long-running… it hasn't come back"); session_search silently returns 0 (#103184).
  • Shared root cause: asynchronous gateway/session state races at the plugin↔core boundary. Multiple projects independently report the same class of bug — a strong signal this is an architectural pattern, not a project-specific defect.

(b) Security boundaries that are either too blunt or bypassable

  • Hermes Agent: E.164 phone-number over-redaction (#68911, needs-decision); ANSI-C quoting approval bypass (#76218, closed); skill egress over-blocking (#143863).
  • ZeroClaw: Caller tool-level approval in bounded delegation (#11138); MITM egress proxy RFC (#12001); write-only credential management (#12373); /mnt/UNC denylist tightening (#12136, breaking).
  • OpenClaw: Unbypassable outbound policy enforcement (#56349, open since March); exec approval card fails to flag mount-point targets (#124306).
  • Shared need: a coherent, auditable model for delegated authority and secret visibility — users want to constrain a compromised agent, not just a misbehaving one.

(c) Provider/model configuration trust

  • QwenPaw: Hub model gateway 502 on Anthropic/MiniMax presets (#8718); context-length exceeded → task aborts (#8312); in-channel /model cannot switch pinned model (#8725).
  • ZeroClaw: OpenCode Go silently using Zen's catalogue (#12412); context-window discovery returns nothing (#12413).
  • OpenClaw: Codex provider/thread mismatch regression (#190563); claude-cli treats transient OAuth refresh-lock as terminal (#156442).
  • Shared need: predictable, inspectable model selection — users are losing trust when providers silently mismatch catalogues or fail opaque.

(d) CJK/i18n gaps (currently OpenClaw-specific but a category-level risk)

  • OpenClaw: CJK bigram tokenizer (#170997) and sessions_search returning 0 for CJK (#140736). No peer has surfaced this yet — a signal that other projects are under-serving non-English users, likely a latent issue as adoption grows.

  2. Hermes Agent — highest sustainable maturity: balanced flow, daily canary cadence, security campaign closing bugs same-day.

7. Trend Signals

Extracted from cross-project community feedback — actionable for AI agent developers:

1. Delivery reliability is the new feature bar. Across OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and QwenPaw, silent loss of background/long-running work is the highest-emotion complaint ("hasn't come back," "stuck pending," "task aborts"). Developers should treat durable, observable async delivery with explicit acknowledgment/retry as a first-class primitive, not an afterthought. The recurring deliveryStatus/notify_on_complete/session_search family suggests the industry lacks a standard contract here.

2. Gateway event-loop/state concurrency is an architectural ceiling. OpenClaw (#119720, #182369) and Hermes Agent (#94455, #149248) independently hit session-state races and memory pressure under scale. For new projects: isolate persistence from the serving loop early (ZeroClaw's Rust runtime and QwenPaw's channel isolation offer partial templates). Retrofitting is expensive — OpenClaw has carried #119720 since August.

3. The security model is shifting from "policy" to "isolation." The most forward-looking proposals (ZeroClaw MITM proxy, write-only secrets, bounded-delegation approval; Hermes exec-wrapper peeling; OpenClaw unbypassable outbound policy) all point the same direction: assume agent compromise, not just agent misbehavior. Developers building multi-agent/tool-using systems should design secret-visibility boundaries and delegation-approval inheritance upfront — this is becoming table stakes, not enterprise upsell.

4. Over-blocking is as damaging as under-blocking. User pain is now bidirectional: redaction that hides legitimate E.164 numbers (#68911), skill egress blocks that kill documented curl calls (#143863). Design per-profile/per-skill exceptions into security primitives from day one. The "guard too blunt" refrain is a predictable second-order effect of security hardening — plan for the tuning surface.

5. Provider abstraction is a trust surface. Silent catalogue mismatches (ZeroClaw/Zen-vs-Go), context-window discovery failures, and opaque model pinning (QwenPaw #8725) erode user trust. Ship inspectable provider resolution (what catalogue, which context window, why this model) and self-recovery paths.

6. Release cadence is a reliability lever, not just a marketing event. OpenClaw's fixes sitting on main but absent from stable (#177063→#185085) directly inflate user-visible P1 volume. Hermes Agent's canary-per-day cadence keeps fixes in user hands fast. Stable backporting is a higher-ROI activity than net-new features for projects at OpenClaw's scale — a directly transferable lesson.

7. Non-English support is a latent, underserved risk. Only OpenClaw surfaces CJK tokenization problems — which may mean peers simply haven't been stress-tested by CJK-heavy users yet. Given QwenPaw's messaging-channel focus (WeChat/Feishu/DingTalk), expect i18n search/tokenization to become a cross-project requirement in the next two quarters.

8. First-time contributors are a strategic asset. QwenPaw's fast issue→fix conversion (first-time contributors filing PRs for #8718, #8727, #8709 within 24h) illustrates the highest-leverage community pattern. IronClaw's unanswered #8170 (a specific, low-cost, high-quality contribution) is the counter-example: squandering a willing contributor is a compounding cost. Projects should instrument "time-to-first-response on external contributions" as a health metric.

Bottom line for decision-makers: The category is consolidating around reliability + security semantics rather than feature breadth. OpenClaw leads in scale and integration surface but pays for it in stability debt and release lag; Hermes Agent and ZeroClaw demonstrate that flow efficiency and architectural security can be competitive advantages even at lower volume; QwenPaw shows that responsive maintainership converts release regressions into community goodwill. The next 1–2 release cycles will likely be decided less by who ships the most features and more by who reliably delivers background work, keeps secrets out of agent reach, and gets fixes into stable fastest.

The most-discussed items (by comment activity) cluster on security architecture and delegation semantics:

The core tension: when a bounded child agent inherits tools from a caller's registry, must it honor the caller's approval requirements? This builds on #10937.

  2. Issue #12001 — RFC: MITM egress proxy to control what the agent can access and to keep secrets hidden from the agent (1 comment, type:rfc). Explicitly framed as a material change to the security model.

Severity Item Component Summary

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Issue #12373 — Write-only WebUI credential management + scoped secret references. Already has PRs #12402 and #12408 → strong candidate for next release.
  • Issue #11138 — Caller tool-level approval in bounded delegation. status:accepted → likely to land as design + implementation incrementally.
  • Issue #12416 — ADR-016 holding-crate exception for host-mediated WASM plugin wake dispatch (zeroclaw-runtime, RuntimeAgentWakeBackend, zeroclaw:plugin/dispatch.wake). Architecture/plugin-system enabling work.
  • Issue #12415 — OIDC RP-initiated logout for dashboard. Small, well-scoped, identity/access topic — plausible quick win.

Prediction: The secrets/credential management cluster (#12373 + #12402/#12408) and the provider catalogue fixes are the most likely to appear in the next version; the MITM proxy and delegation-approval items are larger, cross-cutting efforts likely tracked across multiple releases.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed by real users:

  • Provider configuration confusion (noralane, #12412/#12413): the OpenCode Go provider silently using Zen's catalogue and failing context-window discovery creates an untrustworthy model-selection experience — a degraded, hard-to-diagnose class of problem for anyone relying on accurate context windows.
  • Session/identity leakage (clumbo, #12415): operators expect sign-out to sign out — the silent OIDC re-login undercuts security expectations for shared or managed dashboards.
  • Secret handling anxiety (CastelloBrancoTecnologia, #12373; LaurensBosscher, #12001): multiple independent users are asking for credentials that operators can set but not read, and egress controls that hide secrets from the agent entirely. This is a consistent, security-literate user base.
  • Delegation trust (Audacity88, #11138): users building multi-agent/delegated workflows need explicit, documented approval-inheritance semantics.

Overall sentiment: engaged and security-conscious. Feedback is precise and architectural rather than vague complaint — a sign of a sophisticated contributor/user base, but also of rising expectations around the security model keeping pace with the agent's capabilities.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  • PR #9746 — per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search. Open since 2026-08-04 (~3+ months), priority:p1, risk:high, distinguished contributor, needs-author-action, XL. Touches identity-access, memory backend, channel core/telegram/discord. Long-lived and high-impact — deserves a clear path to merge or a decision.
  • PR #12140 and PR #12136 — both risk:high, needs-author-action; #12136 is breaking. They've been open since late October; breaking security changes need timely review to avoid stale rebases and surprise breakage.
  • PR #12240 — cron --agent reassignment persistence, risk:high, needs-author-action (since 2026-11-05). A correctness fix that's quietly waiting.
  • Issue #11138 — status:accepted but still open since 2026-09-26; the delegation-approval design needs a resolution to unblock dependent work.

Note: The needs-author-action label appears on several high-risk PRs — the bottleneck here is author response, not maintainer review, which is a healthier failure mode but still slows the security-hardening pipeline.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-14

Generated: 2026-11-14 01:24 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project AI Infrastructure Report — 2026-11-14

1. Ecosystem Overview

The ecosystem is in a hardening-over-expansion phase: no project shipped a feature release in the window except llama.cpp's v1.0.0, and four of six digests lead with stability, correctness, or migration stories. Hardware fragmentation is the dominant tax — SM120 (consumer Blackwell) is simultaneously the top theme for vLLM and SGLang and both report it partly broken, while AMD (ROCm/gfx942/gfx950/gfx1151) and edge accelerators (Hexagon, Ascend, MLU) absorb an outsized share of new kernel work. Meanwhile the agent tooling surface is where silent correctness bugs are concentrating: tool-call parsers (Ollama, vLLM), fallback configs (LiteLLM), and KV-cache dtype bugs (vLLM) all produce wrong output without errors. The strategic kernel race has a clear direction — vLLM is migrating off Marlin to Humming for FP4/FP6/FP8 formats, and Unsloth is bringing INT8 attention to diffusion DiTs — while llama.cpp's v1.0.0 signals that local runtimes are formalizing their APIs like production infrastructure.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Notable open issues (top severity / tracker) Notable open/moving PRs Release status Trajectory
vLLM SM120 CUDA graphs broken for DSv4.1 (#56892); FP8 silent KV corruption (#41343); SM8x DSv4-Flash blocked (#50576, 130 comments); Humming migration tracker (#65560) KV connector fixes (#62916, #58525, #67532); tree-shaped draft verification (#64844); Engram pool (#67539); AWQ MoE configs (#66488) No release in 24h; in-review API removal mamba_cache_mode (#63830) Heavy on correctness + new-format kernels; hardware bring-up lagging
SGLang Scheduler double free hang (#42508); Blackwell B200 Xid 13 crashes (#46203); FP8 Marlin nondeterminism (#45000); sm_120 unusable OOTB (#49209) Prefill CP for DS-V4.1 on MI355X (#44730); SM90 FP4 KV attention (#43852); GQA decode fix (#47802) No release in 24h; 1.0 tracker declares stability release (#50045) Explicit stability pivot; AMD prefill story advancing
llama.cpp Tokenizer stack overflow (#27783, open); CUDA mul_mat_vec_f race (#32235, fix open); Vulkan NaN/forever-fence issues (multiple) HIP MMQ tuning (#30021, #30022, #32224); Vulkan coopmat2 GATED_DELTA_NET ~40% (#32111); cgroup-aware threads (#30267) v1.0.0 shipped — breaking public-API removal; --spec-draft-p-min semantics change Mature release; backend work AMD/edge-weighted
Ollama Qwen3.5/3-Coder tool-call corruption (#19694, new); cloud Mimo tool-call flood (#19672); ZDR vs cached-pricing ambiguity (#17489) VRAM accounting/GPU splitting (#19632); auto num_ctx (#13619); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash MLX (#19667) No release in 24h Consolidating runtime + hardening parsers; cloud quality questions open
LiteLLM Gemini intermittent 503s (#50434); budget-reservation leak without DB (#45907); non-HttpOnly cookie carrying proxy key (#36997) Rust router core as only core (#51396); MCP passthrough auth (#49261, #51756); ParallelLoggerV2 port (#51526) v1.108.8 LTS (+ dev .111, maint .106.10) Rust migration + strict validation = breaking behavior
Unsloth ROCm 7.14/MI300X flash-attn backward (#17548); mmap forced in 0.1.917-beta (#17605); GPU idle after update (#17663) Diffusion DiT INT8 attention (#17718); slot-KV persistence (#17121, closed); benchmarks page (#11808) No release in 24h; 0.1.917-beta flagged as regressiony Studio GUI + diffusion inference expansion; beta rough

Two deltas worth calling out: vLLM and SGLang each carry multiple open silent-correctness bugs, while LiteLLM and Ollama's bugs are mostly availability/validation. llama.cpp is the only project with a shipped breaking release, and Unsloth is the only one where the beta channel itself is cited as a deployment hazard.

3. Model Support Race

Leaders by discipline:

  • DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 family — vLLM is the broadest but not the fastest: it has Engram pool sharding (#67539), DSpark spec-decode fixes (#65647), and KV-connector paths in flight, yet Ampere (SM8x) support for V4-Flash remains blocked and SM120 graph capture is broken. SGLang has the deeper hardware-specific wins: FP4 packed main-KV attention on SM90 (#43852) and prefill context-parallel on MI355X (#44730). Ollama is entering via MLX with a mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint (#19667); Unsloth has a community DS-V4.1 torch.compile re-enable (#17660). Net: vLLM leads on feature breadth, SGLang leads on AMD/FP4 depth, nobody has clean Ampere or SM120 coverage.
  • Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 hybrids — vLLM carries ROCm gfx950 optimization trackers for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; llama.cpp's Vulkan GATED_DELTA_NET coopmat2 (~40%) targets exactly this hybrid family; Ollama owns the tool-parsing surface (and its bugs).
  • Multimodal / vision — llama.cpp registered Granite 4 Vision conversion and has open Vulkan GLM-OCR failures; Ollama's MLX PR includes vision; vLLM's Qwen-VL FP8 KV bug (#41343) is the cautionary example.
  • Diffusion / image-video — Unsloth is alone here, with INT8 DiT attention covering MiniMax-H3, FLUX.3 klein, and video DiTs on sm75–sm120 + gfx1151.

Verdict: Nobody leads universally. SGLang is ahead on new-hardware kernel depth; vLLM on model-format breadth; llama.cpp on GPU-agnostic coverage (by volume of backends) but not on frontier models. The gap that matters commercially is Ampere: a large installed base of A100/A800 fleets still cannot run DSv4-Flash on either major engine.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort splits along backend lines, which is itself the signal:

Area vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Unsloth
Quantization kernels Marlin→Humming migration for INT4/8, FP8, MXFP8/4, NVFP4, MXFP6 AITER pin splits (gfx1250); FP4 KV on SM90 Hexagon IQ2_XXS/NVFP4; OpenCL Q4_K GEMM; HIP few-row WMMA (RDNA3.5) INT8 DiT attention w/ Hadamard rotation (NVIDIA + Strix Halo)
KV cache Connector correctness (engine-ID, block size, cross-PP); CUDA checkpoint/restore RFC (#34303) Unified Memory roadmap (#49944): one GPU arena for full+SWA KV, recurrent & request state Slot KV persistence (via Unsloth) —
Batching / graphs Tree-shaped draft verification (#64844); mixed prefill-decode 6× gap (#44806) bs-1 decode graph regression (#49900); breakable prefill CUDA graphs (#45369) — —
Distributed serving KV disaggregation/Mooncake multi-node fixes DP attention tail-graph fixes (#49170) Hexagon multi-device split —
Non-kernel wins Spec-decode logit cutoffs (#66534); engram pool over NVLink/RDMA AR-fusion symmetric buffer writes (#50002) Jinja template overhead (#32023); cgroup-aware threads Slot-KV reload avoidance (#17121)

Reading the table: vLLM and SGLang are competing on kernel formats and memory arbitration; llama.cpp is grinding GPU-specific MMQ/coopmat paths (AMD/Intel) plus hexagon/Adreno edge kernels; Unsloth is vertically integrating inference speed into a GUI training product. KV cache is the new battleground — SGLang's Unified Memory roadmap and vLLM's checkpoint/restore RFC are both trying to solve cold-start and fragmentation, but neither ships a unified memory slab yet. Note the inverse finding: at low batch, SGLang's graph specialization (#49900) and llama.cpp's small-Metal-offset class bugs show CUDA graphs have become a correctness liability, not just a perf lever.

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Project Role in stack Differentiator vs peers
Serving engine (GPU, datacenter) vLLM High-throughput multi-model serving, KV disaggregation, spec-decode Breadth of quant formats + most model checkpoints; most exposed to hardware-bring-up bugs
Serving engine (GPU, datacenter) SGLang Serving engine with the most aggressive new-hardware kernel work (SM90 FP4, AMD gfx950) Deeper hardware/format specialization; 1.0 betting on stability + named errors
Local/edge runtime llama.cpp Single-binary, CPU/GPU/special-accelerator inference; now also a server control plane (daemon, Unix socket, cgroup threads) Broadest backend matrix (CUDA/HIP/Metal/Vulkan/Hexagon/OpenCL); v1.0 API freeze
Local/edge runtime + model distribution Ollama Package manager + runtime for local models, plus cloud throughput Ease-of-use; cloud layer introduces compliance/quality questions it does not fully control
LLM gateway LiteLLM Unified API/proxy across providers, auth, budgets, MCP gateway Cross-provider normalization + cost governance; Rust migration trades leniency for strictness
Fine-tuning / training Unsloth Fast fine-tuning + GUI Studio/Desktop, expanding into inference (GGUF, diffusion) GUI + low-VRAM training; only project owning diffusion DiT inference

Key layering observation: the boundaries are eroding. llama.cpp is building server-infrastructure features (daemon, sockets, cgroup awareness); LiteLLM is building a router core in Rust; Unsloth is embedding inference into a training GUI; Ollama is a local runtime with a commercial cloud. The only clean separation left is gateway (LiteLLM) vs engine (vLLM/SGLang). For stack design, treat llama.cpp's v1.0 API and LiteLLM's Rust core as new contracts, not feature additions.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Consumer/workstation Blackwell (SM120) is the current weakest link, and it's a revenue tier now. vLLM (#56892, #47130, #47436) and SGLang (#49209, #33422) both report SM120 broken or slow, with vLLM explicitly recommending pinning to 0.23.0. If you're buying RTX PRO 6000 fleets, validate on your exact build before committing.
  2. Silent correctness is the top systemic risk, and it clusters in the serving → agent boundary. vLLM's fp8_e5m2 Qwen-VL corruption (#41343), SGLang's FP8 Marlin nondeterminism with overlap scheduler (#45000), Ollama's Qwen tool-call parser corruption (#19694), and LiteLLM's fallback hard-fail (#51396) all either produce wrong output or fail in ways downstream retries can't detect. Recommendation: add output validation at the gateway, not just at the engine.
  3. Speculative decoding is being refined, not expanded. vLLM (tree-shaped verification #64844), llama.cpp (--spec-draft-p-min now skipped for sampled drafts), Unsloth (benchmarks page sweeping MTP/ngram/DSpark/DFlash) all show spec-decode moving from "acceptance rate" to "acceptance correctness and tuneability." Flag: llama.cpp's behavior change means tuned p_min settings may now be inert.
  4. AMD and edge accelerators are where compounding perf gains are landing, but ecosystems are less mature. ROCm 7.14 + MI300X flash-attn backward is broken (Unsloth #17548); SGLang's gfx1250 needs a separate AITER pin with no automated CI (#47562); vLLM has multiple active gfx942/gfx950 trackers. The direction is right; the reliability isn't yet. Re-measure if you evaluated ROCm 3–6 months ago.
  5. Agent workloads are exposing low-concurrency and small-batch pathologies. SGLang's bs-1 decode being slower than bs-2 (#49900), Ollama's Mimo tool-call storm (#19672), and LiteLLM's budget-reservation leak (#45907) all hit single-session or bursty agent patterns disproportionately. Agents are the workload class that tests the least optimized paths of every engine.
  6. Gateways are choosing strictness over leniency, migrating to Rust. LiteLLM's LTS-vs-dev split with breaking validation means app developers should pin :lts until they've audited fallback configs, Bedrock tiers, and Anthropic tool-choice handling. This is the same "named errors over silent coercion" philosophy SGLang is adopting — expect every infra layer to follow.

Watch list for the next 30 days: SM120 fixes on both engines; SGLang's Unified Memory roadmap; llama.cpp v1.0 migration fallout and the spec-decode flag behavior; Unsloth's INT8 DiT kernel merge (#17718) and whether 0.1.917-beta regressions clear before production adoption.

llama.cpp Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Highlights

llama.cpp shipped v1.0.0, its first major version: the deprecated public API is removed and the NextN/speculative-decoding path is promoted to a first-class interface, accompanied by a Hugging Face blog post. Alongside that, the project cleared a very large stale-issue backlog (most items updated today were close-outs), while active engineering work concentrated on HIP/GCN MMQ tuning, Hexagon SSM/quantized kernel coverage, and Vulkan correctness fixes. Notably, the day's backend work is heavily AMD- and edge-accelerator-focused rather than NVIDIA-centric.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v1.0.0 — major release, breaking for API consumers. Deprecated public API removed; NextN/speculative-decoding interface promoted to stable. Downstream projects that still call the old public C API will need to migrate. Release · Hugging Face blog
  • b12364 — speculative decoding semantics change/warning. --spec-draft-p-min is now skipped for sampled MTP and DFlash2 drafts (under rejection sampling, acceptance at a position is 1 - TV(p,q), which the draft's top probability does not reflect). Expect log warnings if you use it; flag behavior may differ. PR #31294
  • Builds b12363–b12374 are rolling incremental builds (Vulkan keepalive, Metal offset fix, Hexagon SSM_SCAN support, CUDA SM103 SASS).

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Hexagon: SSM_SCAN op support — unlocks state-space model layers on Snapdragon NPU, including multi-device splitting. b12373 / #31921
  • Hexagon: IQ2_XXS and NVFP4 quantization — tiled repack layouts, HVX GEMV (n≤4) and HMX paths (n>4), per-tensor NVFP4 scale (PR in merge-ready state). PR #31954
  • CUDA: SM103 SASS added to non-native builds — forward compatibility for newer Blackwell parts. b12367 / #30099
  • HIP: gfx1013 (AMD BC250) registered as RDNA1. PR #32236
  • BF16 support in RMS_NORM on CPU and CUDA — relevant for bf16-native checkpoints. b12366 / #32135
  • Vulkan: TOP_K_MASK op. b12365 / #31544
  • Granite 4 Vision conversion registered (Granite4VisionForConditionalGeneration) — fixes convert_hf_to_gguf.py failures on newer Granite 4 Vision checkpoints. PR #32237
  • Backlog: nemotron_h_moe tensor support still unimplemented. Issue #30798

4. Performance & Optimization

  • HIP GCN MMQ configs tuned; stream_k algorithm tuned for GCN and enabled for specific MMQ configs (benchmarked in the PR). b12370 / #30021 · PR #30022
  • HIP: few-row MMQ via WMMA for RDNA3.5 — a new mul_mat_q_few_wmma kernel using the RDNA3 16×16×16 int8 WMMA path (CUDA version relies on NVIDIA MMA fragments/cp.async, so a separate kernel was required). PR #32224
  • HIP: DPP-based warp sum reduction (__builtin_amdgcn_mov_dpp instead of ds_permute_*), avoiding the LDS bridge. PR #32215
  • Vulkan: coopmat2 GATED_DELTA_NET, with scalar-path row→thread remapping; ~40% average speedup over the prior path (stacked on #30207). Relevant to Qwen3.5/Kimi-linear style hybrid models. PR #32111
  • Jinja template rendering overhead reduction — removes accidental builtin-table copies, shrinks Value storage, cuts temporary allocations, avoids string copies. Directly affects chat-template-heavy llama-server workloads. PR #32023
  • Hexagon buffer/mmap stacking improvements — combined queue/fence buffers, thread-count-based queue sizing, host-side buffer stacking to avoid IOVA fragmentation. b12368 / #32144
  • OpenCL: optimized Q4_K non-MoE GEMM bin kernel for Adreno X1. PR #30948
  • cgroup-aware default thread count for llama-server — caps math threads by effective CPU quota instead of host CPU count, preventing oversubscription in containers. PR #30267

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. Metal: mul_mv destination offset 32-bit overflow → silent unwritten output slices when im * ne0 * ne1 > INT32_MAX (large batched outputs). Fixed in b12374 by promoting offset math to uint64_t. PR #32221
  2. Metal: per-file mmap mapping spans CPU-resident tensors → a 27 GiB lazy-read table between GPU tensors counted against the GPU working set, causing OOM on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Closed/stale. Issue #29465
  3. CUDA: shared-memory data race in mul_mat_vec_f warp reduction — multiple threads per warp writing partial results. Fix PR open. PR #32235
  4. CPU AMX mul_mat incorrect batching (since #19925) — no 2D weight broadcast over batched src1, mis-scaled byte offsets → garbage output with ≥2 parallel sequences and SIGSEGV in tileloadd. Affects llama-server -np on Sapphire Rapids. Closed/stale — verify on your build. Issue #29670
  5. llama-server tokenizer stack overflow — unicode_regex_split_stl recurses per character for the o200k/GPT-4o pre-tokenizer; ~26k-character unbroken runs crash the process. Still open. Issue #27783
  6. glm5-next + --spec-type draft-dflash aborts on first request: GGML_ASSERT(t_layer_inp[il] != nullptr) — architecture never sets t_layer_inp. Open. Issue #30093
  7. Vulkan: all-NaN logits on Radeon 680M, disappears with integer dot product disabled; present since b10343. Open. Issue #31509
  8. Vulkan: GLM-OCR vision encoder garbage output on Intel Arc A380 for full-page images (CPU and SYCL correct). Open. Issue #31836
  9. Vulkan: spin-forever in ggml_vk_wait_for_fence when the driver never reports device loss after a GPU fault (RTX 4090, open kernel module). Open. Issue #29926
  10. --split-mode tensor instability: dual Intel B70 SYCL memory leak during generation (closed, 28 comments), and a hard machine reboot mid-generation on 2× RTX A6000 (closed). Worth tracking if you use tensor split in production. Issue #27845 · Issue #29549
  11. Termux Vulkan builds fail shader optimization (Invalid capability operand: 5447). Open. Issue #28234
  12. /infill endpoint accepts out-of-range token IDs that /completion rejects — input-validation gap. Closed/stale. Issue #29458
  13. Server sleep race with --sleep-idle-seconds — request arriving during the falling-asleep window strands queued tasks and crashes on model unload. Fix PR open. PR #30012
  14. MCP server does not handle non-text tool results. Closed/stale. Issue #28783
  15. iGPU: CPU-resident layers allocated from the Vulkan host buffer, consuming device memory. Open. Issue #31538

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Treat v1.0.0 as a migration event, not a routine bump. If you link against llama.cpp directly or use bindings that wrap the public C API, budget for a compatibility pass before adopting. Server/CLI users are largely unaffected by the API removal but should validate speculative-decoding behavior.
  • Speculative decoding needs re-tuning. The p_min change means the cutoff is deliberately not applied to sampled MTP/DFlash2 drafts. If you tuned --spec-draft-p-min for acceptance-rate gains, re-benchmark — the flag may now be effectively inert on those draft types.
  • Server-mode is getting operationally serious. The daemon + Unix-socket control plane (ACL instead of API key) PR #31489, cgroup-aware thread defaults PR #30267, and the sleep-race fix PR #30012 all point toward containerized/Kubernetes deployment. The sleep-idle crash in particular is a real hazard for scale-to-zero setups — track that PR if you use --sleep-idle-seconds.
  • Two unresolved crash-class bugs affect common agent workloads: (a) tokenizer stack overflow on long unbroken token runs — adversarial or code-heavy prompts can kill the server, so add input-length guards at the gateway layer; (b) the /infill token-ID validation gap — do not forward untrusted token arrays to that endpoint.
  • Batching on Intel AMX is not fully trustworthy. The -np multi-sequence corruption on Sapphire Rapids is severe if real; validate with your own concurrency tests before relying on AMX variants for parallel serving.
  • AMD is where the performance work is landing. RDNA3.5 few-row MMQ and GCN MMQ/stream_k tuning are incremental but compounding; if you evaluated ROCm inference a few months ago, it is worth re-measuring.
  • Vulkan remains the least predictable backend. Fourteen of the notable open issues involve Vulkan across Intel, AMD, NVIDIA and Termux. Prefer CUDA/Metal/HIP for production paths; keep Vulkan for edge and desktop convenience, and pin builds.

  • [PR #19667] mlx: add DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and host-backed table lifecycle — Open. Implements the publisher's mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint in MLX, including host-backed engrams, compressed sparse attention, vision, batched decode, and chat/tool rendering. Shares host-backed tensor mapping with Qwen 3.8 Flash Next and accounts for host-resident weights in model admission. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19667

  • [PR #19688] cmake: support compatible binary MLX-C and XGrammar — Open. Lets packagers supply MLX-C and XGrammar binaries independently of the Ollama build; relevant for downstream distributors (Homebrew, distro maintainers). https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19688

  • [Issue #17748] AMD Radeon 780M Vulkan regression (≥0.32.10) — Closed after updates today. Users reported radv/amdgpu: Not enough memory for command submission / ErrorDeviceLost on larger models under the Vulkan backend, with identical hardware/config working on earlier versions. Worth verifying against your current pinned build if you deploy on RDNA3 iGPUs. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17748

4. Performance & Optimization

  • [PR #19632] llm/server: Fix VRAM accounting and GPU splitting — Open. Addresses multiple VRAM accounting defects that caused models to be incorrectly evicted, refuse to load, or spread across GPUs unnecessarily. Consolidates fixes for #19463, #18679, #18349, #16599. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19632

  • [PR #13619] Auto-size num_ctx to VRAM budget (#12353) — Open. Automatically sizes the context window to available GPU VRAM, targeting the common failure mode where an over-large num_ctx causes VRAM overflow and a costly fallback to CPU inference. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/13619

  • [PR #18181] api: clamp keep_alive durations that overflow int64 — Open. Prevents a keep_alive value large enough to overflow int64 nanoseconds from wrapping negative, which currently causes the scheduler to immediately expire the runner. Low severity, but relevant if you construct keep_alive programmatically. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18181

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity for agent/application workloads:

  1. [Issue #19694] Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Coder parsers: tool-call arguments corrupted or calls lost — OPEN, new today, no fix PR yet. Affects model/parsers/qwen3coder.go and model/parsers/qwen35.go on v0.40.15; qwenTagRegex unchanged on main. Failure depends on content and stream chunking. High impact for anyone shipping tool-calling agents on Qwen3. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19694

  2. [Issue #19672] Cloud: mimo-v2.6-pro — tool-call flooding storm in agentic sessions — OPEN. Single assistant turn emits hundreds of near-identical tool calls, fills the transcript with duplicates, and renders sessions unusable. Reporter flags it as a possible upstream defect and asks which checkpoint is served. Questionable whether an Ollama-side fix is possible; worth escalating to the cloud team. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19672

  3. [Issue #17904] ornith-1.5:35b identifies as Claude — CLOSED. Model claims to be Claude (Anthropic) in response to identity questions. Not fatal, but publishing an undisclosed fine-tune of an Anthropic model as a distinct model is a licensing/compliance problem if you ship it in products. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17904

  4. [Issue #9247] CUDA: unspecified launch failure — CLOSED. Long-standing report of CUDA error: unspecified launch failure on GPU inference (workaround: CPU-only mode). Closed today with 4 comments. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/9247

  5. [Issue #17489] Cloud "cached input" pricing vs. Zero Data Retention — OPEN. User asks how $0.30/M cached input pricing reconciles with a ZDR promise, citing the Kimi K3 model page. Unanswered; potentially material for anyone relying on the ZDR guarantee when routing sensitive workloads to Ollama Cloud. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17489

  6. **[PR #19689] model/parsers: drop whitespace after in later chunks** — **OPEN**. DeepSeek3 and olmo3-think parsers only trim post- whitespace when the tag and whitespace arrive in the same chunk; in practice \n\n arrives separately, so streamed content begins with "\n\n". Cosmetic-to-moderate depending on your output handling. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19689

  7. [PR #19266] server: retry /compact after 413 by dropping images and old items — OPEN. Long Codex sessions containing screenshots can currently fail to compact against Ollama Cloud. Related to #19155. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19266

  8. [PR #19686] api: preserve unmodeled tool schema keywords — CLOSED. Tool JSON Schemas lost keywords (default, minimum, etc.) because the Go struct only models type/description. Relevant if you send rich schemas and rely on validation constraints downstream. https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19686

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin your parser version carefully if you use Qwen3.5 or Qwen3-Coder for tools. #19694 landed today with no fix PR; tool-call argument corruption under streaming is exactly the kind of silent failure that produces malformed agent actions. Consider short-lived feature flags or response validation until a patch ships.
  • Mimo-v2.6-pro on Cloud is unsafe for multi-turn agents until #19672 is triaged. Add circuit breakers on repeated tool-call emissions if you route to it.
  • VRAM accounting fixes are landing but not yet merged. If you run multi-GPU and have suffered from unexplained evictions or unnecessary tensor splits, PR #19632 is the one to watch; consider testing against a fork if it's blocking.
  • num_ctx is about to get smarter. PR #13619 auto-sizing removes a common footgun for users who don't know their GPU's budget. If you manage model loading programmatically, expect semantics to shift.
  • Tool-schema fidelity is improving (#19686 closed), but until it ships, do not rely on default/minimum/maximum surviving the Ollama layer if you validate downstream.
  • Compliance: Issues #17904 (Anthropic-derived model) and #17489 (ZDR vs. caching) both warrant a check against your own publishing or data-handling policy before they surface as customer questions.
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Highlights

LiteLLM shipped an LTS patch (v1.108.8) alongside continued v1.111.0 dev iterations, but the day's developer attention is dominated by the newly Rust-only router core — issue #51396 confirms malformed fallbacks/max_fallbacks payloads now hard-fail with HTTP 500 instead of degrading gracefully. A separate cluster of Gemini translation bugs (intermittent 503s, snake_case system_instruction serialization) is drawing sustained commentary and remains unfixed. MCP gateway auth and cost-accounting correctness continue to generate the highest-volume PR activity.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

  • v1.108.8 (LTS) — Latest LTS patch; the lts image tag now points here. Cosign verification uses key from commit e82a3c6. Pull ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:lts.
  • v1.111.0-dev.2 / dev.1 — Ongoing dev line, no notable API surface changes called out.
  • v1.106.10 — Maintenance release, cosign-signed.

⚠️ Behavioral breaking changes landing (fix PRs merged, not yet released):

  • Rust router core is now the only core — requests with non-list fallbacks/context_window_fallbacks/content_policy_fallbacks or non-integer max_fallbacks now raise ValueError → HTTP 500 instead of being silently coerced. See #51396 (closed).
  • Bedrock service tiers — requests for tiers Bedrock cannot serve will now return 400 rather than silently running at a different tier. #50516.
  • Anthropic malformed tool choices — now return 400 instead of 500 or silent auto-selection. #46188.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Soniox STT v6 — stt-async-v6 and stt-rt-v6 released Nov 3; v5 models deprecate Dec 15, 2026. Cost map PR requested. #50934.
  • Ollama text-to-image — Feature request for first-class litellm.image_generation(model="ollama/...") support (currently returns empty ImageResponse.data). #28026.
  • Vertex Claude versioned IDs — fix in flight to resolve correct max_tokens (e.g., Haiku 4.5 at 64000 vs. the hardcoded 128000 fallback that Vertex rejects). #40376.
  • Shared input/output context windows — feature request to let model_map express a single combined context budget (newer Gemini-era models). #51723.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • Ollama non-default host latency — get_runtime_model_info ignores the request api_base and falls back to localhost:11434, incurring ~8s of silent connect timeouts per completion on remote Ollama deployments. Open, tagged stale. #37041.
  • Parallel first-request race — burst of parallel requests to a freshly-started proxy worker could fail with internal schema errors during response-object construction. Fix builds chat/text/embedding schemas eagerly. #51733.
  • Rust CustomLoggerV2 — callback contract and proxy request-scope binding PR opened; five port PRs stacked behind it. #51526.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. LLM translation: OpenAI-like servers force /responses — cannot force /chat/completions even with openai/ prefix; breaks Reflection.AI and any server supporting only chat completions. Closed; verify fix. #51547.
  2. Budget-reservation leak with no DB logger — when custom_auth_run_common_checks reserves spend with no database_url, the reservation sticks until TTL and the next request fails. Fix PR open. #45907.
  3. Retried budget reset erases rollover-capped spend — reset job commits end-user spend per page before the window advance; a later failure re-walks the same users and drops carried spend. Closed. #50898.
  4. Gemini intermittent 503 / APIConnectionError — alternating service-unavailable and server-disconnected errors through the translation layer. Open, highest comment count today. #50434.
  5. Gemini custom api_base sends system_instruction not systemInstruction — snake_case causes duplicate protobuf oneof assignment on some Gemini-compatible proxies. Open, stale. #37028.
  6. Bedrock Llama native streaming undercounts prompt tokens — provider prompt_token_count and cumulative generation_token_count are dropped; prompt usage logs as zero. Open. #51456.
  7. Admin UI session cookie is non-HttpOnly JWT carrying proxy key — key claim holds the caller's real proxy key. Security-relevant; open, stale. #36997.
  8. Upstream MCP server URL leaked in public model hub modal — exposes internal infra URLs to end users. Closed. #30472.
  9. _read_request_body returns {} on parse failure — large (~1.9MB) embedding batches hit ProxyModelNotFoundError: model=None. Closed. #32114.
  10. Budget reservation leak (dup of #45907 category) and sticky session routing — router ignores session affinity and re-routes to different endpoints. Open. #50029.

Active fix PRs worth tracking: Transcribe pass-through soundfile import (#45379, closed), Anthropic Responses adapter preserving [text, tool_use, text] ordering (#45478), Generic Guardrail API now writes rewritten tool_calls back to client (#50413), and MCP true_passthrough returning 401 on expired upstream token (#49261).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin to LTS (:lts / v1.108.8) for production if you rely on lenient input handling — the Rust router core no longer coerces malformed fallback configs, and Bedrock/Anthropic invalid inputs now 400 instead of degrading.
  • Audit your fallbacks config as a list of lists before upgrading past v1.109 — non-list shapes will hard-fail requests with 500.
  • Gemini users: expect intermittent 503s and be aware custom api_base proxies may reject the system_instruction key; consider disabling system messages via that path until #37028 lands.
  • If you run without database_url (SDK-only or stateless proxy), check whether budget reservations are being released — #45907's leak can poison subsequent requests until TTL.
  • Bedrock Claude on Invoke with computer-use/browser-use tools is currently broken due to placeholder tool naming; fix PR #51756 addresses it — avoid those toolsets on Bedrock until released.
  • MCP gateway operators: expired upstream OAuth tokens currently surface as opaque failures on tools/list; #49261 restores a proper 401 to trigger client re-auth.
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth Digest — 2026-11-14

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases in the last 24 hours, but PR/issue traffic is heavy and centered on Unsloth Studio/Desktop (the new GUI surface). Headline items: an INT8 attention kernel for diffusion DiTs spanning NVIDIA sm75–sm120 and AMD gfx1151 (#17718), a fix for the DeepSeek-V4.1 torch.compile regression (#17660), and a Gemma 4 chat training fix that was incorrectly stripping <bos> (#17678, closed). On the bug side, a mmap regression in 0.1.917-beta (#17605) and ROCm 7.14 / MI300X flash-attention backward failures (#17548) are the most consequential for production users.

2. Releases & Breaking Changes

None — no releases published in the reporting window.

Version-adjacent regression worth flagging: [Unsloth 0.1.917-beta] ignores an explicit --load-mode none and forces mmap, causing excessive RAM/SSD usage (#17605). Reported on Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB) with a 97 GiB EXL3 GGUF. If you're pinned to 0.1.916, defer the upgrade until fixed.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • Diffusion DiT INT8 attention kernel — in-progress PR covering MiniMax-H3 / H3-Image, FLUX.3 klein, and video DiTs; targets NVIDIA sm75 / sm80 / sm86 / sm89 / sm120 and AMD gfx1151 (Strix Halo, Linux + Windows). Uses a 16-point Hadamard rotation before INT8 Q·Kᵀ (#17718).
  • DeepSeek-V4.1 (community port) — re-enables torch.compile now that unsloth_zoo aligns checkpoint recompute behavior (#17660, closed).
  • Gemma 4 chat training — restores the leading <bos> token that format_and_template_dataset was stripping for all Gemma-name-matched models; the previous behavior was correct for Gemma 1/2/3/3n but wrong for Gemma 4 (#17678, closed).
  • AMD NPU (FastFlowLM/Lemonade) — context sizing now scales to free RAM instead of a flat 8192 tokens, capped at 65536 (#17511, closed).
  • Qwen-Image 2.1 edit mode — Edit toggle now works on shared-library sd.cpp builds by scanning stable-diffusion.{dll,so,dylib} for the edit marker (#17720).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • INT8 attention for diffusion DiTs (#17718) — the main perf item; enablement for both NVIDIA and Strix Halo (gfx1151) matters because DiT attention is a primary bottleneck at high resolutions / long video contexts.
  • Slot KV persistence across GGUF reloads (#17121, closed) — a Context Length change no longer triggers a full re-prefill; only the paths that previously persisted slot KV (idle unload, media swap, /unload) are honored. Directly improves long-chat latency after any reload event.
  • Downstream pip install isolation in Studio (#17626, open) — prevents user pip install from mutating Studio's own venv; a stability win as much as a perf one (no more accidentally upgraded huggingface_hub breaking model loads).
  • Benchmarks page (#11808, open, >3000 LOC) — will sweep speculative decoding (MTP/ngram/DSpark/DFlash), KV cache type, context length, parallel slots, and GPU offload on the currently loaded GGUF. Useful once it lands for tuning real deployments.
  • huggingface_hub 1.18+ partial download progress (#17715, open) — count in-flight .partial files so multi-GB image/video loads don't appear stalled.

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity:

  1. ROCm 7.14 / MI300X (gfx942): stride assertion in _scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_backward requiring MATH fallback (#17548, open). Training-side correctness/perf blocker on AMD MI300X with recent ROCm. No fix PR linked.
  2. mmap forced despite --load-mode none on 0.1.917-beta (#17605, open). Regression vs 0.1.916; causes elevated RAM and disk churn. No fix PR linked yet.
  3. config.json missing after HF upload of a fine-tuned Llama 3 8B (#368, closed). Old issue, re-touched 2026-11-13 — worth knowing if you saw the same OSError; the resolution path should be verified in the thread.
  4. GPU idle after engine update; only "Restore installation" recovers inference (#17663, open). v0.1.917-beta, RTX 5090 Laptop. Recovery works but is buried in a UI flow.
  5. Docker: audio.cpp update fails with "invalid cross-device link" (#17638, open). Affects the provided Studio docker image (host Ubuntu 26.04).
  6. Studio Transcribe: MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize fails on long audio because max_tokens is never sent (#17598, open).
  7. Combined CSV export loses chat boundaries (#17655, open) — round-trip import merges N chats into one.
  8. Web UI file picker hides Markdown exports in Import chats (#17651, open).
  9. Docker image tags do not track the latest release (#17470, closed).
  10. Mobile (Cloudflare) chat updates not reconciled in Desktop embedded WebView (#17689, open) — v0.1.917-beta, RX 9070 XT + ROCm.

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Pin off 0.1.917-beta if you rely on explicit load modes or Docker. Two independent regressions (mmap forcing, Docker cross-device link) plus a GPU-idle-after-update bug suggest this beta is not production-ready for edge-GPU deployments.
  • AMD users: treat ROCm 7.14 + MI300X training as unstable until #17548 clears. The MATH fallback is a correctness-preserving workaround but will tank throughput on flash-attention-heavy training loops. Strix Halo (gfx1151) inference looks healthier — the new INT8 DiT kernel explicitly targets it.
  • If you build on Studio's chat/session layer: the slot-KV persistence fix (#17121) and the upcoming token-usage limiter (#16500) change long-session and quota behavior. The token limiter returns HTTP 429 after the allowance, with a one-time override — design your retry/backoff paths accordingly if you proxy Studio.
  • If you embed Studio in your own infra: #17626 matters — until it lands, any pip install from Studio's Terminal or Python tool can corrupt the runtime environment. Sandbox or block that path.
  • Diffusion app builders: once #17718 lands, DiT inference (MiniMax-H3, FLUX.3 klein, video) should see meaningful speedups on both NVIDIA (down to Turing sm75) and Strix Halo. Worth tracking the merge commit before benchmarking.
  • Hub search ergonomics improve: #17721 adds owner/model and owner/ filtering to Hub search, matching the feature request in #17665 — useful if you're building model-picker UIs mirroring Studio's behavior.
